data.long_meaning: From Hebrew 'zedek' (righteous) + 'yah' (God). Signifies 'the righteousness of God' or 'justice of the Lord'. The name Zedekiah carries the meaning “Righteousness of the Lord” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zedekiah usually hope their child will grow to embody righteousness of the lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Zedekiah" is significant in Jewish and Christian history as it is the name of two prominent figures in the Bible. The first, and most notably, is the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile in 586 BC. King Zedekiah's reign was marked by disobedience to God and eventual capture by Nebuchadnezzar, which led to the downfall of the Judean monarchy and the beginning of the Babylonian exile. The name "Zedekiah" thus came to symbolize royalty, leadership, and the consequences of disobedience to God in biblical and Jewish culture.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name "Zedekiah" represents the call to live a life rooted in righteousness and obedience to God, as demonstrated by the name's meaning 'the righteousness of God'. In the Bible, Zedekiah the king is a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and avoiding disobedience, as his downfall ultimately came from turning away from God. As such, the spiritual significance of the name "Zedekiah" lies in its encouragement for individuals to strive for righteousness and obedience to God, as exemplified by biblical figure King Zedekiah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zedekiah: Righteousness of the Lord. A king who sought God's guidance but ultimately led Judah into captivity. Symbolizes the paradox of human aspiration for righteousness amidst imperfection.

biblical_reference.note: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, who reigned during the Babylonian exile.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Zedekiah was a king of Judah, the last king before the Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem in 586 BC. The name Zedekiah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During his reign, Jeremiah the prophet warned Zedekiah of impending doom, but he refused to listen. Zedekiah's rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar II led to the siege and eventual conquest of Jerusalem.

historical_references.reference: Zedekiah was also the name of a descendant of King David who was a priest during the reign of King Josiah.
historical_references.context: He was instrumental in reinstating the temple worship after a period of apostasy. However, he was eventually assassinated by the Babylonians during their invasion of Judah.
